rv.q: Jeremy Herrin's three-and-a-half-hour production suffers from terminal bloat, it is undeniably blessed in its leading old lady, whom Manville shapes as a couture-crafted entity beyond good and evil.
In Kushner's hands, however, Dürrenmatt's brisk script mushrooms into a production that is almost four hours long with two intervals.
But for all its opulence, this self-indulgent show lacks heart and, at four hours, is far, far too long.
It is by no means a flawless evening, but the sheer scale of the production, unimaginable outside of the massively resourced National Theatre, fills gaps in the dramatic writing.
Manville's whiplash-smart assuredness in a role that calls for a star and gets one proves one of the few invigorating aspects of a long and spirit-depleting evening.
